The Good Shepherd Discourse
SHEP-erd
noun phrase
From the Greek ho poimēn ho kalos, “the good shepherd,” the I AM saying in which Christ declares He layeth down His life for the sheep.

📖 Biblical Definition

In the tenth chapter of John the Lord Jesus said, I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep (Joh 10:11), and twice over, I lay down my life for the sheep (Joh 10:15). He set Himself forth as the Shepherd who knows His own and is known of them, even as the Father knoweth Him and He the Father; and His knowing and His dying are particular: not for sheep in general, but for the sheep, His sheep, given Him of the Father. He marked the difference between His own and the rest: ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me (Joh 10:26, 27). To these He gives eternal life, and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of His hand (Joh 10:28). The dictionary marks the good shepherd discourse as the great Johannine witness to particular, definite redemption: Christ laid down His life not in a vague intention toward all, but effectually for the sheep the Father gave Him, every one of whom He calls by name, keeps to the end, and raises up at the last day. So the Scripture teaches that the cross was no failed offer but a finished and effectual work, by which the Shepherd purchased His flock, knows each of them, and brings them safely home, that not one of them is lost.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The I AM discourse in which Christ declares He layeth down His life for the sheep, teaching particular and definite redemption.

THE GOOD SHEPHERD DISCOURSE, the I AM saying of John 10.

The good shepherd giveth, and layeth down, His life for the sheep.

He knows His own and is known of them, as the Father knoweth Him.

His sheep hear His voice, and He gives them eternal life.

None shall pluck them out of His hand, for He keeps them to the end.

📖 Key Scripture

Joh 10:11 — "I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep."

Joh 10:15 — "As the Father knoweth me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for the sheep."

Joh 10:27 — "My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:"

Joh 10:28 — "And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A saying of Christ corrupted by the universal-atonement reading; it teaches that Christ laid down His life effectually for His own sheep, not for all in general.

expand to see more

The good shepherd discourse is pressed by some into a universalist or general-atonement mould, as though Christ laid down His life equally for every man without distinction, so that the cross secured nothing in particular and only made salvation possible for all alike. But this is to read past the very words the Shepherd spake; for He says not that He died for the world without distinction, but I lay down my life for the sheep, and again, ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep.

The Scripture answers the universalist reading on its own ground. Christ’s dying is particular and effectual: He giveth His life for the sheep, He knoweth them, He calleth them, and to them, and not to the goats, He giveth eternal life with the promise that they shall never perish. Were the atonement for all without distinction, then either all must be saved (which Scripture denies) or Christ’s blood failed for the many who perish (which dishonours His finished work). The Reformed and confessional doctrine of definite redemption is the plain sense of the discourse: the Shepherd purchased His flock, knows each by name, and loseth none. This is no narrowing of grace but the strength of it, for a redemption that actually saves is greater than a redemption that only might.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Greek for “the good shepherd,” the saying names Christ as He who layeth down His life for His own sheep.

expand to see more

The Good Shepherd Discourse — Greek ho poimēn ho kalos, the good shepherd.

It is the I AM saying of the tenth chapter of John.

The good shepherd layeth down His life for the sheep.

He knoweth His own and is known of them, and they hear His voice.

He giveth them eternal life, and none shall pluck them from His hand.

Usage

"Like a shepherd who dies to save his flock, Christ laid down His life for the sheep."

"My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me."

"None shall pluck them out of His hand, for the Shepherd keeps His own."
